description_short: Filter metals ALE Table 2 for high-rate processes (EPC ≥ 2 Å/cycle) and list material, direction, chemistries, EPC, temperature, and cycle time.

paper.title: Anisotropic/Isotropic Atomic Layer Etching of Metals

tables_modeled.label: Table 2
tables_modeled.description: Summary of anisotropic and isotropic metal ALE chemistries, including direction, modification and removal chemistry, EPC, process temperature, and cycle time.

comparisons.table_source: Table 2 (metals ALE processes) from the metal ALE review.

properties_used.label: Material
properties_used.role: Identifies the metal material being etched (e.g. W, Co, Pt).

properties_used.label: Direction
properties_used.role: Specifies whether the ALE process is anisotropic or isotropic.

properties_used.label: Reaction
properties_used.role: Captures the surface modification / reaction chemistry used in the first ALE step.

properties_used.label: Removal
properties_used.role: Captures the removal / desorption chemistry used to remove the modified layer.

properties_used.label: Process Temperature (°C)
properties_used.role: Etching process temperature, relevant to thermal budget and compatibility with device stacks.

properties_used.label: Time of cycle
properties_used.role: Time per ALE cycle, allowing basic throughput considerations.

properties_used.label: EPC (Å/cycle)
properties_used.role: Etch-per-cycle rate; used here to filter for high-rate metal ALE processes (EPC ≥ 2 Å/cycle).

aggregation.description: This Easy Query operates row-wise: it filters individual ALE processes by EPC threshold without aggregating across materials.

output_shape.description: One row per metal ALE process with EPC ≥ 2 Å/cycle.
columns: reaction: modification chemistry used in the first step.
removal: removal chemistry used in the second step.
epc: numeric etch-per-cycle rate (Å/cycle), parsed from text.
process_temp: process temperature (°C) as recorded in the comparison.

postprocessing_notes.interpretation: The result isolates the highest-rate metal ALE chemistries in the table. Comparing EPC alongside direction, chemistry, temperature, and cycle time helps identify promising candidates for high-throughput, anisotropic or isotropic metal etching under realistic process conditions.
